observations: Two sewing machine stands are shown outdoors on a cracked concrete surface.
The stand on the left has a blue painted top surface with a wavy pattern.
The stand on the right has a brown wood-grain patterned top surface.
Both stands have the same black metal frame design, including the treadle mechanism and footrest.
The top surface of the blue stand in photo 2 has a ruler printed on it.
The top surface of the brown stand in photo 3 has a glass insert in the center.
The stands appear to be in a used condition.

claims.evidence: The items shown are the base frames for sewing machines, which are used for both sewing and weaving.

risks.risk: The stands may be missing the actual sewing machines.
risks.proof: Photos of the complete sewing machines on the stands.

risks.risk: The treadle mechanism may be broken or not working.
risks.proof: A video showing the treadle being operated.

risks.risk: The glass insert in the brown stand may be cracked or missing.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the glass insert in the brown stand.
risks.if_unproven: as having a damaged glass insert

risks.risk: The metal frame may be rusted or structurally weak.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the joints and the underside of the frame.

proof_requests: Photos of the actual sewing machines on the stands.
A video of the treadle mechanism in operation.
A photo of the glass insert in the brown stand.
Close-up photos of the metal frame to check for rust.
response.reason: The items are clearly identifiable as sewing machine stands. They can be priced at their worst-case value as empty stands.
